human_review: Commission check
Whether a short, missing or charged-back commission is really owed, and approving any inquiry draft before a person sends it to the carrier.
Producer pay and bonuses
Every producer pay correction and bonus estimate, against the producer and carrier agreements, before anyone is paid.
Agency bill and trust account
Every trust shortfall, transfer, refund and remittance; the principal or accountant decides, and only a person moves money.
Renewals and retention
Whether to remarket a renewal or call a lapsed client; licensed staff talk to the client, and the agents give no coverage advice.
Service desk
Certificates, endorsements, policy differences and claims: a licensed person checks the policy and issues or corrects anything.
Licensing and E&O file
The state settings (CE hours, appointment and document rules) and each licence, appointment or missing-form finding, confirmed by the agency.
Data clean-up
Every client merge and every correction in the agency system, made by staff after checking.
Book summary
Any use of the figures in a sale or valuation; they summarise your files and are not an appraisal.
Whole agency
All of the above; each draft waits for one named person to approve it, and a person sends it.
Agency network rollout
Each member agency's own settings, findings and approvals, by that agency's staff.
common_problems: A carrier paid new business at the renewal commission rate (12% instead of 15%).
A policy written months ago never appeared on a commission statement.
A carrier took back the full commission on a mid-term cancellation instead of the unearned part.
The premium trust account was short of the premiums owed to carriers, and rent had been paid from it.
A certificate shows a higher limit, a waiver or an additional insured that the policy does not have.
A renewal 24% higher with a review logged but no remarket.
A producer wrote business with a carrier while the appointment was pending or terminated.
A premium finance loan was funded and the money was never passed on to the carrier.
reaches_the_model: When an assistant calls a check, its model sees the result: amounts, rates, dates, statuses, carrier, producer and CSR names, lines of business and policy numbers. Client and insured names and client numbers are replaced by pseudonyms; birth dates become the year; driver's licence numbers, SSNs, addresses, phones and e-mails are removed; --phi strict also hides policy and claim numbers and VINs. Notes people type (cancellation reasons, change requests, bank descriptions) are sent as typed. Results go to whatever model the user's assistant uses, so for client data use a model covered by your own agreements or a local model.
rules_maintained: No state law or carrier rule is built in. Continuing-education hours, trust-account allowances, commission schedules, producer splits, bonus grids and document checklists are settings files your agency writes, dates and confirms; the agents read them on every run, so a change takes effect at once. Day counts and limits (reinstatement days, renewal windows, loss-ratio limits) are defaults you can change on each run. Export layouts and line-of-business words ship with the agents and are updated in new versions; you can add your own column names and carrier aliases yourself.
